Non-friable material

Bonded asbestos removal, fibro, eaves and roof sheeting

Removal of non-friable asbestos: fibro cladding and linings, eaves and soffits, corrugated roof sheeting, wet area linings, vinyl floor tiles and fencing. The common form, and the one most Sydney properties built before 1990 carry somewhere. Carried out by licensed asbestos removalists in line with SafeWork NSW requirements. Tell us where the sheeting is, and we will quote removal, disposal and clearance in one line.

0456 220 552

Removal by licensed asbestos removalists. Max holds demolition licence AD214737

Before anything starts

Six things have to be settled first, and not all of them are ours

Most jobs that run late run late on this list rather than on the work itself. Each line says who owns it.

  1. 01

    Survey result in hand

    Who Max, through an accredited laboratory

    What it is, where it is and what condition it is in. Removal is quoted from this, not from a look.

  2. 02

    Licence class confirmed

    Who Max, with the removalist

    Bonded material has its own licence class. If the survey finds friable material as well, the scope changes and so does the contractor.

  3. 03

    Notification where required

    Who Max

    Licensed removal work is notifiable, with a notice period set by the regulation.

  4. 04

    Occupants and neighbours informed

    Who You, with our help

    Exclusion zones, signage and the days the work happens. Worth doing early rather than on the morning.

  5. 05

    Power and access arranged

    Who You

    Removalists need power and a clear path for wrapped material to leave the property intact.

  6. 06

    Disposal booked

    Who Max

    A facility licensed to receive asbestos, booked before the material comes off rather than after.

The detail

What makes a bonded job straightforward or not

  • Condition. Intact sheeting comes off whole. Weathered, cracked or previously damaged material has to be treated far more carefully and sometimes as friable.
  • Where it is. Eaves and a roof are a different job from wet area linings behind tiles or vinyl under three later floor coverings.
  • Whether it is fixed or fastened. Sheeting screwed to battens comes off differently from sheeting glued to a substrate.
  • Access. Material has to leave wrapped and intact. A rear roof with no side access changes the method and the hours.
  • Whether the building is occupied. More separation, more signage and usually more hours.
  • How much there is. The survey gives a quantity, and the quantity is what the disposal cost is built from.

What we need to quote it

The address
So we can look at access and what is around it

Your dates
What has to be finished by when, and what is waiting on it

We attend the site before quoting anything substantial.

Found damaged material instead?

Weathered, broken or previously disturbed sheeting may be treated as friable, which is a different licence class with an enclosure and air monitoring throughout.

Before you book

What people ask about this one

What does bonded mean?
The asbestos fibres are held in a matrix, usually cement, and do not release readily while the material is intact and undisturbed. That is what separates it from friable material, which can be crumbled by hand when dry.
Can I remove a small amount myself?
There are limits in NSW on what an unlicensed person may remove, and they are small. Before you consider it: the disposal still has to go to a licensed facility, and breaking the material up is how a cheap job becomes contaminated soil.
Do I get a clearance certificate?
Where the work requires it, yes, issued by an independent licensed assessor who is neither the removalist nor us. Keep it. It is what proves the property was handled properly.
How long does it take?
A garage roof can be a day. A whole house of fibro cladding, eaves and wet areas is a week or more. The survey is what turns that into a real answer.
What happens to the material?
Double wrapped, labelled, transported and buried at a facility licensed to receive asbestos. It does not go to a general waste facility and it is not recycled.

Get a quote

Send a photograph of what you have found

A picture of the material and the approximate age of the building tells us whether it is likely bonded, and what a survey would need to cover.
